labels.expectedFinding: A vocabulary gloss supports no grammar target; mapping it to the pronoun target would record pronoun support (and postpone independent credit) whenever the learner only needed the word.
por qué (preposition + interrogative) introduces the question; porque (conjunction, 'because') introduces the reason.
Names of days, months and seasons are common nouns and are written in lowercase as a general rule.
mediodía denotes a moment (noon, the central hours of the day); medio día denotes a duration (half a day).

Spanish has two plural forms of address, vosotros and ustedes; the vosotros reflexive imperative is levantaos/duchaos and the ustedes one levántense/dúchense, so both «Sentaos» and «Siéntense» fit depending on the unstated relationship.
Participles of -uir verbs (construido, incluido) carry no tilde (-ui- is a diphthong in llanas); the hint's 'always' rule and examples are false.
«ayer tarde» is perfectly appropriate (DPD), alongside ayer por la tarde.
One thing given to several people is «se la/se lo»; moving the plural onto the direct-object pronoun («se las») is strongly rejected in European Spanish.
Ukrainian ви is used to address two or more people or, politely, one person (СУМ); Spanish distinguishes usted, vosotros and ustedes, and the prompt does not say which applies.
«Idos» is the recommended vosotros imperative of irse, but the Academia also considers the widespread variant «iros» valid.
In the 12-hour model the part of the day is specified with de la mañana / de la tarde / de la noche; «a las ocho de la tarde» is 20:00.
The imperfecto presents past facts in their course, the indefinido as finished; without context both views of 'my grandfather worked in a factory' are possible.
«coger el autobús/ascensor» and «tomar…» are both correct; coger is only to be avoided in some American countries.
Teach before testing: plural person forms (including vosotros) are not in the taught list, so the item assesses an untaught person form.
dio, vio, fue (and di, vi, fui) are written without a tilde because they are orthographic monosyllables.
Ukrainian «слово» is a neuter noun (СУМ: «СЛОВО, а, с.»), so the demonstrative must be «це», not feminine «ця».
With la mayoría de + plural noun, both singular and plural verb agreement are adequate (plural more usual); no attribute/predicative here.
In -ducir verbs the stem c becomes j in the indefinido: condujo, not «condució».
«tres euros con veinte» is 3,20 €; the key accepts 3,02 and the correct amount would only be unresolved.
The perfecto refers to a past action within a period not yet finished, often an implicit one such as 'the current day'; the prompt does not fix that period, so «llamé» cannot be ruled out.
Interrogative dónde carries a tilde, and omitting the opening question mark is considered a spelling error.
le is the indirect-object pronoun for a singular recipient of either gender; the sentence offers two singular candidates and nothing selects one.
Compound tenses use the haber form «ha» (with h) + participle: «ha llamado», not «a llamado».
a ver and haber are homophones (they sound the same); an isolated clip cannot show which spelling is intended.
Only regular -ar indefinido forms are taught at this point; «fui» is an irregular form of ir/ser that is not taught yet and is not a regular -ar form, so it cannot be assessed under this target.
In the 12-hour model the part of the day is given by de la mañana/de la tarde/de la noche; without it «a las ocho» can be 8:00 or 20:00.
The RAE considers «andé» incorrect; the correct form is «anduve».
la is the feminine singular direct-object pronoun; it does not identify which of two feminine singular referents is meant.
The transcript states the shop does not open on Sundays; the key marks the opposite answer correct.
An audio-only meaning question must not display the transcript; showing it turns the listening target into reading and removes the support decision from the learner.
«de nada» is a completely correct courteous reply when someone thanks you.
In ir a + infinitive the preposition a must never be dropped in careful usage: va a llover, not «va llover».
Feminine nouns beginning with stressed a take «el» in the singular but stay feminine, so adjectives agree in the feminine: el agua fría.
té (noun 'infusion') carries a diacritic tilde; te (pronoun) does not.
The personal pronoun mí (after a preposition: para mí) carries a diacritic tilde, unlike the possessive mi.
Existential haber is impersonal and stays singular: «había muchas personas», not «habían».
lo is the direct object for a male person; le is also admitted for male persons (leísmo de persona), more often in the singular.
«hecho» is the irregular participle of hacer (FundéuRAE lists it with roto as an irregular participle).
imprimir has two participles; impreso and imprimido are both adequate in compound tenses (impreso more frequent).
freír has two participles; both freído and frito are adequate in compound tenses («He freído/frito un huevo»).
